summary: Read-only review complete: 5 findings. No edits, builds, tests, network access, or .env reads.

findings.title: Customer passkey deletion leaves derived grants and registrations usable
findings.detail: Only admin deletion invalidates pending authorization. An attacker can authenticate with a compromised customer passkey, obtain a management grant or registration challenge, then complete registration after the owner deletes that passkey. Deletion changes neither the password fingerprint nor the attacker's session; branches E/B never recheck the authorizing credential. Engine support: packages/api/src/auth/session.ts:111-154 resolves sessions independently of authentication credentials, and routes/customer-tokens.ts:140-145 explicitly revokes authorization during recovery rather than relying on credential removal.
findings.fix: Under the customer lock, invalidate pending management grants and registration challenges on passkey deletion, or bind them to an authorizing credential whose continued validity is checked at consumption. Test deletion between proof, grant consumption, and registration verification.

findings.title: Admin deletion preserves passkey-derived step-up authority
findings.detail: Deleting pending challenges does not clear step_up_at. An attacker who logged in and stepped up with the compromised passkey can wait for its deletion, then request a new registration challenge and enroll a replacement during the remaining five-minute window. The TOTP fingerprint remains unchanged. Engine support: packages/api/src/auth/admin-session.ts:231-232 stores only a timestamp; routes/admin-helpers.ts:124-127 checks only identity kind and timestamp freshness; db/schema-core.ts:188-196 records no step-up credential provenance.
findings.fix: Invalidate passkey-derived step-up authority atomically with deletion. Either track and revalidate its credential provenance or clear affected sessions' step_up_at conservatively. Test starting a new registration after deletion, not merely completing an already-pending challenge.

findings.title: Rollback TOTP disable and re-enable can resurrect invalidated passkeys
findings.detail: The fingerprint detects current state, not a recovery event. During rollback, disable TOTP and re-enable the same logical secret before re-upgrading: the original fingerprint returns, and the previous image never deleted the passkeys. Contrary to the assumed 'new secret', packages/api/src/routes/admin-security.ts:87-96 accepts a caller-supplied secret once TOTP is absent, and auth/admin-staff.ts:104-110 persists it without preventing reuse. Lazy invalidation cannot observe the intervening NULL state.
findings.fix: Make invalidation durable across previous-image writes, for example through an additive database trigger that deletes passkey credentials and pending authorization on TOTP disable. Rehearse disable followed by re-enrollment with the same secret, while preserving sealing/unsealing compatibility.

findings.title: Admin session liveness is incompatible with customer sessions
findings.detail: The shared contract applies admin-staff.ts's expiry/idle predicate to customers. That predicate uses ADMIN_SESSION_IDLE_HOURS and coalesce(last_seen_at, created_at) (packages/api/src/auth/admin-staff.ts:75-81). Customer sessions never update last_seen_at: auth/session.ts:71-79 initializes only expiry, and :139-151 renews only expires_at. With the default 12-hour admin idle limit, legitimate 30-day customer sessions become unusable for passkey management and the restructured password-change route. Customer resolution also checks legacy_expires_at (:134-135), which the proposed admin predicate omits.
findings.fix: Specify separate locked liveness predicates for admins and customers. Preserve customer expiry, legacy expiry, owner/store binding, and renewal policy without imposing the admin idle limit. Cover old-but-live customer sessions and expired legacy sessions.

findings.title: Unchanged profile mutations retain the reverse session/customer lock order
findings.detail: Restructuring password change alone does not eliminate the cycle with new passkey transactions. packages/api/src/routes/account.ts:353-360 calls me() and then updates customer; auth/session.ts:147-151 can first update and lock the renewable session. Concurrent passkey management locks customer first and then that session. Each transaction can therefore wait on the other's row. Address creation at account.ts:415-424 similarly renews the session before inserting a customer foreign key.
findings.fix: Include existing session-renewing customer mutations that subsequently acquire customer locks, including profile update and address creation, in the ordering repair. Move their renewal into a completed transaction or acquire the owner first, then add deterministic concurrency coverage against passkey management.
